edges.description: GARP dysfunction produces abnormal endosomal or vesicular-body morphology in patient fibroblasts.
Endosomal trafficking disruption is mechanistically linked to downstream sphingolipid and lysosomal homeostasis abnormalities in GARP deficiency.
Endosomal, lysosomal, lipid, and Golgi-processing disruption converges on severe neurodevelopmental disease and can include hepatic involvement.

nodes.description: Patient fibroblasts show swollen and abnormally numerous CD63-positive vesicular bodies consistent with disrupted intermediate recycling or late endosomal trafficking downstream of VPS53/GARP dysfunction.

evidence.reference_title: VPS53 mutations cause progressive cerebello-cerebral atrophy type 2 (PCCA2).
evidence.snippet: Immunofluorescent microscopy demonstrated swollen and abnormally numerous CD63 positive vesicular bodies, likely intermediate recycling/late endosomes, in fibroblasts of affected individuals.

nodes.description: VPS53-related GARP dysfunction causes a severe pontocerebellar or cerebello-cerebral neurodevelopmental disorder and, in at least one report, liver disease and deafness.

evidence.reference_title: VPS53 mutations cause progressive cerebello-cerebral atrophy type 2 (PCCA2).
evidence.snippet: Progressive cerebello-cerebral atrophy (PCCA) leading to profound mental retardation, progressive microcephaly, spasticity and early onset epilepsy

evidence.reference_title: Hepatic manifestations in VPS53-related pontocerebellar hypoplasia type 2E: A case report.
evidence.snippet: Pathogenic variants in VPS53 are associated with pontocerebellar hypoplasia type 2E (PCH2E), characterized by microcephaly, severe neurodevelopmental impairment and epilepsy.

evidence.reference_title: Hepatic manifestations in VPS53-related pontocerebellar hypoplasia type 2E: A case report.
evidence.snippet: the classic phenotypic features along with liver disease and deafness

nodes.description: GARP deficiency reroutes or misbalances sphingolipid trafficking, causing accumulation of sphingolipid intermediates and lysosomal dysfunction in model systems and PCCA2 patient fibroblasts.

evidence.reference_title: The GARP complex is required for cellular sphingolipid homeostasis.
evidence.snippet: GARP deficiency leads to accumulation of sphingolipid synthesis intermediates, changes in sterol distribution, and lysosomal dysfunction.

evidence.reference_title: The GARP complex is required for cellular sphingolipid homeostasis.
evidence.snippet: PCCA2 fibroblasts exhibited increases in sphingosine, sphinganine, and ceramides compared with control fibroblasts.

nodes.description: Biallelic VPS53 variants disrupt the GARP complex, impairing retrograde recycling of endocytic vesicles to the Golgi.

evidence.snippet: Autosomal recessive PCCA type 2 is caused by VPS53 mutations.
